title: Twice-yearly lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis: both phase 3 trials, reported as incidence rate ratios, with the randomised and the counterfactual comparisons kept apart
question: In the two phase 3 lenacapavir prevention trials, what is the incidence of HIV acquisition with lenacapavir relative to the randomised oral active control, and separately relative to the background incidence estimated in the screened population?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the validator's numeric list. Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from. No measured input is stored that the staged sources do not carry, which is why this object has no person-years field. DERIVED transforms of stored values -- the log point and log standard error of a ratio -- are stored and are not claimed to appear in any source; an earlier wording said no figure at all was stored beyond the sources, which was false of those fields.
_estimand_rule: The estimand is an incidence rate over person-time. Events and participants are stored because they are published, and NOT in the shape of a table of participants with and without an event, so that no risk ratio can be computed from them.
completeness_statement: FULL BUILD: both phase 3 trials of this intervention are held and reported. Nothing was cited and dropped.

handbook.decision: REPORT each trial separately; compute NO pooled estimate
handbook.conformance: ONE reason is sufficient and it is arithmetic rather than judgement: PURPOSE 1's rate ratio is exactly zero, so it has no logarithm, and the generic inverse-variance method that sections 10.3.3 and 10.8 prescribe for combining rate ratios operates on log ratios. There is nothing to give it. Section 10.4.4 is cited for what it actually covers -- rare events in two-by-two data, where it recommends the Peto method and warns that adding a half to each cell 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference'. That warning is about CELLS and these are RATES, so it is cited as the nearest guidance rather than as governing; a reviewer objected to an earlier version that cited it as though it governed, and was right. A Peto odds-ratio synthesis on the participant counts IS computable and is not performed for two stated reasons: it would silently change the estimand from the rate ratio both trials published to an odds ratio on participants, and both trials allocated unequally, which is the condition 10.4.4 identifies as biasing that method. The population difference between the trials is recorded as clinical diversity under 10.10.1 and is NOT claimed to be independently sufficient -- an earlier version did claim that, which is stricter than the Handbook, since 10.10.3 treats declining to synthesise as a judgement about whether an average would mislead and random-effects models exist precisely to carry such diversity.

handbook.decision: REPORT each trial separately; compute NO pooled estimate, and never combine this with the randomised contrast
handbook.conformance: The comparator is not a randomised group. Section 3.2.3 distinguishes the kinds of comparison a review may make, and an estimate against an incidence modelled in a screened population is not the same quantity as a contrast between two randomised arms: it carries the assumptions of that model and none of the protection randomisation provides. The two are reported as separate outcomes for that reason. No synthesis across trials is computed here either, and the governing reason is the same arithmetic one as for the randomised contrast -- one trial's rate ratio is zero and the generic inverse-variance method of 10.3.3 and 10.8 has no log ratio to take. An earlier version invoked that reason here while citing only the comparison-definition and heterogeneity sections, which did not govern it.

ftaf_vs_background.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. claims_corrected.status: a confusion of two different intervals

claims_corrected.claim: that the oral comparator arms of PURPOSE 1 may be added together
claims_corrected.correction: F/TAF and F/TDF are different drugs randomised as separate groups, and the trial designates only F/TDF as the active control.

primary.poolable_reason: TWO TRIALS, AND THEIR REGISTERED PRIMARY DOES NOT COMPARE LENACAPAVIR AGAINST A RANDOMISED ARM. Registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18. In BOTH trials the registered primary is HIV-1 incidence per 100 person-years measured AGAINST A BACKGROUND INCIDENCE ESTIMATE derived from screened participants by a recent-infection testing algorithm -- PURPOSE 2 (NCT04925752) posts lenacapavir 0.103 against a background of 2.374 from 4634 screened; PURPOSE 1 (NCT04994509) posts lenacapavir 0.000 against a background of 2.407 from 8094 screened. A BACKGROUND RATE FROM SCREENED PARTICIPANTS IS AN EXTERNAL, NON-RANDOMISED COMPARATOR, and pooling two trials on their contrast with it would pool two non-randomised comparisons while presenting the result as a randomised one. AND WHERE THE TRIALS DO CARRY RANDOMISED ACTIVE ARMS, THOSE ARMS ARE DIFFERENT DRUGS: F/TDF in PURPOSE 2, F/TAF in PURPOSE 1. Different comparator, different question. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any trial here is poor -- each is registered and reports its own primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective; both lenacapavir trials in fact report striking results on their own terms. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. THE CRITICISM IS OF THE POOLING AND OF NOTHING ELSE. The registry is a live document and this reads its contents on 2026-08-18; a later amendment could change it.
primary.the_zero_event_arm: PURPOSE 1 posts 0.000 HIV-1 events per 100 person-years in the lenacapavir arm. A zero-event arm requires a continuity correction or an exact method before any ratio can be formed, and house rules permit adding 0.5 ONLY where a cell is zero. THIS IS NOT WHY THE TOPIC CLOSES -- the comparator limb closes it -- but it is recorded because a future attempt to pool these two trials will meet it and should not discover it late.
primary.what_would_make_this_poolable: A pool of the RANDOMISED contrasts would need the two trials to share an active comparator, which they do not. A pool restricted to PURPOSE 2's F/TDF contrast is k=1 and is a single trial, not a synthesis.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In the two phase 3 lenacapavir prevention trials, what is the incidence of HIV acquisition with lenacapavir relative to the randomised oral active control, and separately relative to the background incidence estimated in the screened population?

It examines 2 randomised trials and DOES NOT POOL THEM.

The outcomes sought are Lenacapavir against F/TDF, the randomised active control; Lenacapavir against the estimated background incidence in the screened population; F/TAF against F/TDF, both randomised oral arms; F/TAF against the estimated background incidence.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21._what: The five reporting claims a PRISMA-2020 manuscript needs that are FETCHABLE rather than argued -- each derived from a field here, or stated as an honest absence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_limbs_this_review_refuses: Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 0 are held (none) and 4 are refused with the obstacle named in the evidence (comparison denominator, grade per pool, model output verbatim, rob per result).
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases: PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.that_two_assessors_disagreed_and_where: NO SECOND, INDEPENDENT RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED FOR THIS TOPIC. The judgements were made once. Stated so that single assessment is not mistaken for agreement between two.
